sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ bījair yajñeṣu yaṣṭavyam iti vai vaidikī śrutiḥ ajasaṃjñāni bījāni chāgaṃ na ghnantum arhatha
english: The seers said: The Vedic revelation declares that one should sacrifice in the rites with seed-grains; the grains themselves are called 'aja' — therefore you ought not to slay a goat.

sanskrit: naiṣa dharmaḥ satāṃ devā yatra vadhyeta vai paśuḥ idaṃ kṛtayugaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kathaṃ vadhyeta vai paśuḥ
english: O gods, that is no dharma of the virtuous wherein a living creature is slain. This is the most excellent Kṛta age — how then should a beast be killed?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca teṣāṃ saṃvadatām evam ṛṣīṇāṃ vibudhaiḥ saha mārgāgato nṛpaśreṣṭhas taṃ deśaṃ prāptavān vasuḥ antarikṣacaraḥ śrīmān samagrabalavāhanaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: While the seers were disputing thus with the gods, the foremost of kings, Vasu, came upon that place along his path — that glorious one who roamed the sky, with all his forces and chariots about him.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasāyāntaṃ vasuṃ te tv antarikṣagam ūcur dvijātayo devān eṣa chetsyati saṃśayam
english: Seeing Vasu come suddenly, coursing through the air, the twice-born said to the gods: 'This one will resolve the doubt.'

sanskrit: yajvā dānapatiḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvabhūtahitapriyaḥ kathaṃ svid anyathā brūyād vākyam eṣa mahān vasuḥ
english: 'A performer of sacrifices, the foremost of lords of giving, devoted to the welfare of all beings — how could this great Vasu speak a word that is otherwise than true?'

sanskrit: evaṃ te saṃvidaṃ kṛtvā vibudhā ṛṣayas tathā apṛcchan sahasābhyetya vasuṃ rājānam antikāt
english: Having thus made their agreement, the gods and the seers alike approached King Vasu at once and questioned him at close hand.

sanskrit: bho rājan kena yaṣṭavyam ajenāho svid auṣadhaiḥ etan naḥ saṃśayaṃ chindhi pramāṇaṃ no bhavān mataḥ
english: 'Ho, King! With what should one sacrifice — with a goat, or rather with the herbs? Resolve this doubt of ours; you are held to be our authority.'

sanskrit: sa tān kṛtāñjalir bhūtvā paripapraccha vai vasuḥ kasya vaḥ ko mataḥ pakṣo brūta satyaṃ samāgatāḥ
english: Vasu, joining his palms in reverence, questioned them in turn: 'Which view does each of you hold? Speak the truth, you who are assembled here.'

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ dhānyair yaṣṭavyam ity eṣa pakṣo 'smākaṃ narādhipa devānāṃ tu paśuḥ pakṣo mato rājan vadasva naḥ
english: The seers said: 'That one should sacrifice with grains — this is our position, O ruler of men; but the gods' position favors the beast. Pronounce for us, O King.'

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca devānāṃ tu mataṃ jñātvā vasunā pakṣasaṃśrayāt chāgenājena yaṣṭavyam evam uktaṃ vacas tadā
english: Bhīṣma said: Then Vasu, knowing the opinion of the gods and inclining to their side, spoke these words: 'One should sacrifice with a goat — with the aja.'

sanskrit: kupitās te tataḥ sarve munayaḥ sūryavarcasaḥ ūcur vasuṃ vimānasthaṃ devapakṣārthavādinam
english: At this all those sages, radiant as the sun, grew angry and said to Vasu, seated upon his flying chariot, who had spoken in support of the gods' cause:

sanskrit: surapakṣo gṛhītas te yasmāt tasmād divaḥ pata adya prabhṛti te rājann ākāśe vihatā gatiḥ asmacchāpābhighātena mahīṃ bhittvā pravekṣyasi
english: 'Since you have taken the gods' side, therefore fall from heaven! From this day on, O King, your course through the sky is severed; struck by our curse, you shall cleave the earth and sink into it.'

sanskrit: tatas tasmin muhūrte 'tha rājoparicaras tadā adho vai saṃbabhūvāśu bhūmer vivarago nṛpaḥ smṛtis tv enaṃ na prajahau tadā nārāyaṇājñayā
english: Then in that very moment King Uparicara at once sank downward, the monarch passing into a cleft of the earth; yet by the command of Nārāyaṇa his memory did not desert him then.

sanskrit: devās tu sahitāḥ sarve vasoḥ śāpavimokṣaṇam cintayām āsur avyagrāḥ sukṛtaṃ hi nṛpasya tat
english: But all the gods together, unperturbed, took thought for Vasu's release from the curse, for that deed of the king had been a meritorious one.

sanskrit: anenāsmatkṛte rājñā śāpaḥ prāpto mahātmanā asya pratipriyaṃ kāryaṃ sahitair no divaukasaḥ
english: 'On our account this great-souled king has incurred a curse. We dwellers in heaven must together render him a kindness in return.'

sanskrit: iti buddhyā vyavasyāśu gatvā niścayam īśvarāḥ ūcus taṃ hṛṣṭamanaso rājoparicaraṃ tadā
english: Having resolved thus in their minds and swiftly reached their decision, the lords, glad of heart, then said to King Uparicara:

sanskrit: brahmaṇyadevaṃ tvaṃ bhaktaḥ surāsuraguruṃ harim kāmaṃ sa tava tuṣṭātmā kuryāc chāpavimokṣaṇam
english: 'You are devoted to Hari, the god who befriends the brāhmaṇas, the teacher of gods and demons; well-pleased of soul, he may at will work your deliverance from the curse.'

sanskrit: mānanā tu dvijātīnāṃ kartavyā vai mahātmanām avaśyaṃ tapasā teṣāṃ phalitavyaṃ nṛpottama
english: 'Yet honor must be shown to the high-souled twice-born; their austerity must inevitably bear its fruit, O best of kings.'

sanskrit: yatas tvaṃ sahasā bhraṣṭa ākāśān medinītalam ekaṃ tv anugrahaṃ tubhyaṃ dadmo vai nṛpasattama
english: 'Since you have fallen suddenly from the sky to the surface of the earth, this one favor we grant you, O most excellent of kings.'

sanskrit: yāvat tvaṃ śāpadoṣeṇa kālam āsiṣyase 'nagha bhūmer vivarago bhūtvā tāvantaṃ kālam āpsyasi yajñeṣu suhutāṃ viprair vasor dhārāṃ mahātmabhiḥ
english: 'For as long a time as you must dwell through the fault of the curse, O sinless one, sunk in the cleft of the earth, for just so long you shall receive the well-offered stream of Vasu's draught, poured by the high-souled brāhmaṇas in their sacrifices.'

sanskrit: prāpsyase 'smadanudhyānān mā ca tvāṃ glānir āspṛśet na kṣutpipāse rājendra bhūmeś chidre bhaviṣyataḥ
english: 'By our favoring thought you shall obtain it; let no weariness touch you, nor hunger and thirst, O lord of kings, while you abide in the fissure of the earth.'

sanskrit: vasor dhārānupītatvāt tejasāpyāyitena ca sa devo 'smadvarāt prīto brahmalokaṃ hi neṣyati
english: 'Nourished by drinking the stream of Vasu and replenished in your splendor, that god, pleased by our boon, shall lead you to the world of Brahmā.'

sanskrit: evaṃ dattvā varaṃ rājñe sarve tatra divaukasaḥ gatāḥ svabhavanaṃ devā ṛṣayaś ca tapodhanāḥ
english: Having thus granted the boon to the king, all the dwellers in heaven there — the gods and the seers rich in austerity — departed to their own abodes.

sanskrit: cakre ca satataṃ pūjāṃ viṣvaksenāya bhārata japyaṃ jagau ca satataṃ nārāyaṇamukhodgatam
english: And ever, O descendant of Bharata, he paid worship to Viṣvaksena, and ceaselessly chanted the prayer that had issued from the mouth of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: tatrāpi pañcabhir yajñaiḥ pañcakālān ariṃdama ayajad dhariṃ surapatiṃ bhūmer vivarago 'pi san
english: Even there, O subduer of foes, sunk in the cleft of the earth though he was, he worshipped Hari, the lord of the gods, with five sacrifices at the five appointed times.

sanskrit: tato 'sya tuṣṭo bhagavān bhaktyā nārāyaṇo hariḥ ananyabhaktasya satas tatparasya jitātmanaḥ
english: Then the Lord Nārāyaṇa, Hari, was pleased by the devotion of that virtuous man — one whose devotion was undivided, who was wholly given to him, master of himself.

sanskrit: varado bhagavān viṣṇuḥ samīpasthaṃ dvijottamam garutmantaṃ mahāvegam ābabhāṣe smayann iva
english: The Lord Viṣṇu, the granter of boons, spoke as if smiling to the foremost of the twice-born who stood near him — Garutmān of mighty speed:

sanskrit: dvijottama mahābhāga gamyatāṃ vacanān mama samrāḍ rājā vasur nāma dharmātmā māṃ samāśritaḥ
english: 'O best of the twice-born, greatly blessed one, go at my word: the sovereign king named Vasu, a soul devoted to dharma, has taken refuge in me.'

sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ prakopena praviṣṭo vasudhātalam mānitās te tu viprendrās tvaṃ tu gaccha dvijottama
english: 'By the wrath of the brāhmaṇas he entered the floor of the earth; yet those foremost of brāhmaṇas have been honored. Go now, O best of the twice-born.'

sanskrit: bhūmer vivarasaṃguptaṃ garuḍeha mamājñayā adhaścaraṃ nṛpaśreṣṭhaṃ khecaraṃ kuru māciram
english: 'O Garuḍa, by my command make that foremost of kings, hidden in the cleft of the earth and now moving below, a sky-rover once more — and do it without delay.'

sanskrit: garutmān atha vikṣipya pakṣau mārutavegavān viveśa vivaraṃ bhūmer yatrāste vāgyato vasuḥ
english: Then Garutmān, swift as the wind, spreading wide his wings, entered the cleft of the earth where Vasu abode in restrained speech.

sanskrit: tata enaṃ samutkṣipya sahasā vinatāsutaḥ utpapāta nabhas tūrṇaṃ tatra cainam amuñcata
english: Then the son of Vinatā, lifting him up at once, sprang swiftly into the sky and there released him.

sanskrit: tasmin muhūrte saṃjajñe rājoparicaraḥ punaḥ saśarīro gataś caiva brahmalokaṃ nṛpottamaḥ
english: In that very moment King Uparicara came to be again, and that best of kings went, in his own body, to the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: evaṃ tenāpi kaunteya vāgdoṣād devatājñayā prāptā gatir ayajvārhā dvijaśāpān mahātmanā
english: Thus, O son of Kuntī, even by him, that high-souled one, through a fault of speech and the curse of the brāhmaṇas, a destiny befitting one who offers no sacrifice was incurred — and reversed by the gods' command.

sanskrit: kevalaṃ puruṣas tena sevito harir īśvaraḥ tataḥ śīghraṃ jahau śāpaṃ brahmalokam avāpa ca
english: Solely because he had served the Supreme Person, Hari the Lord, he swiftly cast off the curse and attained the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ te bhūtā mānavā yathā nārado 'pi yathā śvetaṃ dvīpaṃ sa gatavān ṛṣiḥ tat te sarvaṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanā nṛpa
english: All this I have related to you — how the mortals came to be. And how the seer Nārada too went to the White Island, all of that I shall now declare to you; listen with single mind, O King.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca prāpya śvetaṃ mahādvīpaṃ nārado bhagavān ṛṣiḥ dadarśa tān eva narāñ śvetāñ candraprabhāñ śubhān
english: Bhīṣma said: Having reached the great White Island, the venerable seer Nārada beheld those very men — white, radiant as the moon, and fair.

sanskrit: pūjayām āsa śirasā manasā taiś ca pūjitaḥ didṛkṣur japyaparamaḥ sarvakṛcchradharaḥ sthitaḥ
english: He honored them with his bowed head and with his mind, and was honored by them in turn; longing for the vision, supremely given to silent prayer, bearing every austerity, he abode there.

sanskrit: bhūtvaikāgramanā vipra ūrdhvabāhur mahāmuniḥ stotraṃ jagau sa viśvāya nirguṇāya mahātmane
english: With mind made single-pointed, the brāhmaṇa, that great sage, his arms upraised, chanted a hymn to the Universal One, the One free of qualities, the Great Soul.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca namas te devadeva [1] niṣkriya [2] nirguṇa [3] lokasākṣin [4] kṣetrajña [5] ananta [6_116] puruṣa [7] mahāpuruṣa [8] triguṇa [9] pradhāna [10] amṛta [11] vyoma [12] sanātana [13] sadasadvyaktāvyakta [14] ṛtadhāman [15] pūrvādideva [16] vasuprada [17] prajāpate [18] suprajāpate [19] vanaspate [20] mahāprajāpate [21] ūrjaspate [22] vācaspate [23] manaspate [24] jagatpate [25] divaspate [26] marutpate [27] salilapate [28] pṛthivīpate [29] dikpate [30] pūrvanivāsa [31] brahmapurohita [32] brahmakāyika [33] mahākāyika [34] mahārājika [35] caturmahārājika [36] ābhāsura [37] mahābhāsura [38] saptamahābhāsura [39] yāmya [40] mahāyāmya [41] saṃjñāsaṃjña [42] tuṣita [43] mahātuṣita [44] pratardana [45] parinirmita [46] vaśavartin [47] aparinirmita [48] yajña [49] mahāyajña [50] yajñasaṃbhava [51] yajñayone [52] yajñagarbha [53] yajñahṛdaya [54] yajñastuta [55] yajñabhāgahara [56] pañcayajñadhara [57] pañcakālakartṛgate [58] pañcarātrika [59] vaikuṇṭha [60] aparājita [61] mānasika [62] paramasvāmin [63] susnāta [64] haṃsa [65] paramahaṃsa [66] paramayājñika [67] sāṃkhyayoga [68] amṛteśaya [69] hiraṇyeśaya [70]
english: Nārada said: Homage to you, God of gods [1], Actionless [2], Free of qualities [3], Witness of the worlds [4], Knower of the field [5], Endless [6], Spirit [7], Great Spirit [8], the One of three strands [9], Primordial nature [10], Deathless [11], Sky [12], Eternal [13], the Being and Non-being, Manifest and Unmanifest [14], whose dwelling is cosmic order [15], the First and Foremost god [16], Bestower of wealth [17], Lord of creatures [18], Best Lord of creatures [19], Lord of the woodland [20], Great Lord of creatures [21], Lord of vigor [22], Lord of speech [23], Lord of mind [24], Lord of the world [25], Lord of heaven [26], Lord of the Maruts [27], Lord of the waters [28], Lord of the earth [29], Lord of the quarters [30], the First-dwelling [31], Brahmā's chaplain [32], the Brahmā-bodied [33], the Great-bodied [34], the Mahārājika [35], the Fourfold-Mahārājika [36], the Radiant [37], the Greatly-radiant [38], the Sevenfold-greatly-radiant [39], the Yāmya [40], the Great Yāmya [41], the Named-and-Nameless [42], the Tuṣita [43], the Great Tuṣita [44], Pratardana [45], the Wholly-fashioned [46], the One whose will prevails [47], the Un-fashioned [48], Sacrifice [49], Great Sacrifice [50], Origin of sacrifice [51], Womb of sacrifice [52], Embryo of sacrifice [53], Heart of sacrifice [54], Praised in sacrifice [55], Receiver of the sacrificial portion [56], Upholder of the five sacrifices [57], Goal of those who perform the five rites at their times [58], the Pāñcarātrika [59], Vaikuṇṭha [60], Unconquered [61], the Mental One [62], Supreme Master [63], the Well-purified [64], the Swan [65], the Supreme Swan [66], the Supreme Sacrificer [67], Sāṃkhya-and-Yoga [68], the One who reposes in the deathless [69], the One who reposes in gold [70].

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evaṃ stutaḥ sa bhagavān guhyais tathyaiś ca nāmabhiḥ taṃ muniṃ darśayām āsa nāradaṃ viśvarūpadhṛk
english: Bhīṣma said: Praised thus with secret and true names, that Lord, bearer of the universal form, revealed himself to the sage Nārada.

sanskrit: kiṃ cic candraviśuddhātmā kiṃ cic candrād viśeṣavān kṛśānuvarṇaḥ kiṃ cic ca kiṃ cid dhiṣṇyākṛtiḥ prabhuḥ
english: In part pure of self as the moon, in part surpassing even the moon; in part of the color of fire, and in part the Lord shaped like a blazing altar-hearth.

sanskrit: śukapatravarṇaḥ kiṃ cic ca kiṃ cit sphaṭikasaprabhaḥ nīlāñjanacayaprakhyo jātarūpaprabhaḥ kva cit
english: In part the color of a parrot's wing, and in part with the luster of crystal; like a heap of dark collyrium, and somewhere with the radiance of pure-born gold.

sanskrit: pravālāṅkuravarṇaś ca śvetavarṇaḥ kva cid babhau kva cit suvarṇavarṇābho vaiḍūryasadṛśaḥ kva cit
english: And of the hue of a coral shoot, and white in places he shone; somewhere with the gleam of gold, and somewhere like a beryl gem.

sanskrit: nīlavaiḍūryasadṛśa indranīlanibhaḥ kva cit mayūragrīvavarṇābho muktāhāranibhaḥ kva cit
english: Like a blue beryl, and somewhere like the sapphire of Indra; with the sheen of a peacock's neck, and somewhere like a necklace of pearls.

sanskrit: etān varṇān bahuvidhān rūpe bibhrat sanātanaḥ sahasranayanaḥ śrīmāñ śataśīrṣaḥ sahasrapāt
english: Bearing these manifold colors in his form, the Eternal One — thousand-eyed, glorious, hundred-headed, thousand-footed.

sanskrit: sahasrodarabāhuś ca avyakta iti ca kva cit oṃkāram udgiran vaktrāt sāvitrīṃ ca tadanvayām
english: Thousand-bellied and thousand-armed, and somewhere the Unmanifest — uttering from his mouth the syllable Oṃ, and the Sāvitrī that follows upon it.

sanskrit: śeṣebhyaś caiva vaktrebhyaś caturvedodgataṃ vasu āraṇyakaṃ jagau devo harir nārāyaṇo vaśī
english: And from his remaining mouths the god Hari Nārāyaṇa, the self-controlled, chanted the wealth that springs from the four Vedas, the Āraṇyaka.

sanskrit: vedīṃ kamaṇḍaluṃ darbhān maṇirūpān athopalān ajinaṃ daṇḍakāṣṭhaṃ ca jvalitaṃ ca hutāśanam dhārayām āsa deveśo hastair yajñapatis tadā
english: An altar, a water-pot, darbha-grass, gem-like stones, a deerskin, a staff of wood, and the blazing fire that devours oblations — these the Lord of gods, the master of sacrifice, then held in his hands.

sanskrit: taṃ prasannaṃ prasannātmā nārado dvijasattamaḥ vāgyataḥ prayato bhūtvā vavande parameśvaram tam uvāca nataṃ mūrdhnā devānām ādir avyayaḥ
english: Nārada, that best of the twice-born, his own self serene, with restrained speech and purified, did homage to the gracious Supreme Lord; and to him, bowed in head, the imperishable First of the gods spoke:

sanskrit: ekataś ca dvitaś caiva tritaś caiva maharṣayaḥ imaṃ deśam anuprāptā mama darśanalālasāḥ
english: 'The great seers Ekata, Dvita, and Trita came to this place, longing to behold me.'

sanskrit: na ca māṃ te dadṛśire na ca drakṣyati kaś cana ṛte hy ekāntikaśreṣṭhāt tvaṃ caivaikāntiko mataḥ
english: 'But they did not see me, nor shall anyone see me, save the best of the single-minded devotees — and you are accounted single-minded.'

sanskrit: mamaitās tanavaḥ śreṣṭhā jātā dharmagṛhe dvija tās tvaṃ bhajasva satataṃ sādhayasva yathāgatam
english: 'These excellent embodiments of mine were born in the house of Dharma, O brāhmaṇa; worship them ever, and accomplish your purpose as you have come to do.'

sanskrit: vṛṇīṣva ca varaṃ vipra mattas tvaṃ yam ihecchasi prasanno 'haṃ tavādyeha viśvamūrtir ihāvyayaḥ
english: 'And choose a boon from me, O brāhmaṇa, whatever you desire here; I, of universal form and imperishable, am pleased with you this day.'

sanskrit: nārada uvāca adya me tapaso deva yamasya niyamasya ca sadyaḥ phalam avāptaṃ vai dṛṣṭo yad bhagavān mayā
english: Nārada said: 'This day, O god, the fruit of my austerity, my restraints and my observances, has been at once obtained — in that I have beheld you, Lord.'

sanskrit: vara eṣa mamātyantaṃ dṛṣṭas tvaṃ yat sanātanaḥ bhagavān viśvadṛk siṃhaḥ sarvamūrtir mahāprabhuḥ
english: 'This is my utmost boon — that I have seen you, the Eternal: the Lord, the all-seeing, the lion, of every form, the great sovereign.'

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evaṃ saṃdarśayitvā tu nāradaṃ parameṣṭhijam uvāca vacanaṃ bhūyo gaccha nārada māciram
english: Bhīṣma said: Having thus revealed himself to Nārada, son of the Supreme One, he spoke again these words: 'Go, Nārada, without delay.'

sanskrit: ime hy anindriyāhārā madbhaktāś candravarcasaḥ ekāgrāś cintayeyur māṃ naiṣāṃ vighno bhaved iti
english: 'For these devotees of mine, moon-bright, who take no food through the senses, would meditate upon me single-mindedly — let no hindrance arise for them.'

sanskrit: siddhāś caite mahābhāgāḥ purā hy ekāntino 'bhavan tamorajovinirmuktā māṃ pravekṣyanty asaṃśayam
english: 'These greatly blessed ones are perfected; long ago they became single-minded. Freed from darkness and passion, they shall enter into me beyond all doubt.'

sanskrit: na dṛśyaś cakṣuṣā yo 'sau na spṛśyaḥ sparśanena ca na ghreyaś caiva gandhena rasena ca vivarjitaḥ
english: 'He who is not to be seen by the eye, nor touched by the sense of touch, nor smelled by way of scent, and is void of taste —'

sanskrit: sattvaṃ rajas tamaś caiva na guṇās taṃ bhajanti vai yaś ca sarvagataḥ sākṣī lokasyātmeti kathyate
english: 'whom the qualities — goodness, passion, and darkness — do not attend; who is all-pervading, the witness, and is called the Self of the world —'

sanskrit: bhūtagrāmaśarīreṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati ajo nityaḥ śāśvataś ca nirguṇo niṣkalas tathā
english: 'when the bodies of the host of beings perish, he does not perish: unborn, eternal, everlasting, free of qualities, and without parts.'

sanskrit: dvirdvādaśebhyas tattvebhyaḥ khyāto yaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ puruṣo niṣkriyaś caiva jñānadṛśyaś ca kathyate
english: 'Beyond the twice-twelve principles, he who is renowned as the twenty-fifth is the Spirit, the actionless, and is said to be perceived through knowledge.'

sanskrit: yaṃ praviśya bhavantīha muktā vai dvijasattama sa vāsudevo vijñeyaḥ paramātmā sanātanaḥ
english: 'Having entered into whom men become liberated here, O best of the twice-born — he is to be known as Vāsudeva, the Supreme Self, the Eternal.'

sanskrit: paśya devasya māhātmyaṃ mahimānaṃ ca nārada śubhāśubhaiḥ karmabhir yo na lipyati kadā cana
english: 'Behold the greatness and the majesty of the god, O Nārada, who is never tainted by deeds, whether pure or impure.'

sanskrit: sattvaṃ rajas tamaś caiva guṇān etān pracakṣate ete sarvaśarīreṣu tiṣṭhanti vicaranti ca
english: 'Goodness, passion, and darkness — these they declare to be the qualities; these abide in all bodies and move within them.'

sanskrit: etān guṇāṃs tu kṣetrajño bhuṅkte naibhiḥ sa bhujyate nirguṇo guṇabhuk caiva guṇasraṣṭā guṇādhikaḥ
english: 'These qualities the Knower of the field enjoys, yet by them he is not enjoyed: free of qualities, yet the enjoyer of qualities, their creator, and surpassing them.'

sanskrit: jagatpratiṣṭhā devarṣe pṛthivy apsu pralīyate jyotiṣy āpaḥ pralīyante jyotir vāyau pralīyate
english: 'O divine seer, earth is the foundation of the world; earth dissolves into the waters, the waters dissolve into fire, and fire dissolves into wind.'

sanskrit: khe vāyuḥ pralayaṃ yāti manasy ākāśam eva ca mano hi paramaṃ bhūtaṃ tad avyakte pralīyate
english: 'Wind passes into dissolution in space, and space into mind; for mind is the highest element, and that dissolves into the Unmanifest.'

sanskrit: avyaktaṃ puruṣe brahman niṣkriye saṃpralīyate nāsti tasmāt parataraṃ puruṣād vai sanātanāt
english: 'The Unmanifest, O brāhmaṇa, dissolves wholly into the Spirit, the actionless; there is nothing higher than that Spirit, the Eternal.'

sanskrit: nityaṃ hi nāsti jagati bhūtaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam ṛte tam ekaṃ puruṣaṃ vāsudevaṃ sanātanam sarvabhūtātmabhūto hi vāsudevo mahābalaḥ
english: 'For in the world there is no eternal being, moving or unmoving, save that one Spirit, Vāsudeva the Eternal; for Vāsudeva of great might has become the Self of all beings.'

sanskrit: pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiś ca pañcamam te sametā mahātmānaḥ śarīram iti saṃjñitam
english: 'Earth, wind, space, water, and fire as the fifth — these great elements, when joined together, are designated a body.'

sanskrit: tadāviśati yo brahmann adṛśyo laghuvikramaḥ utpanna eva bhavati śarīraṃ ceṣṭayan prabhuḥ
english: 'He who enters into that, O brāhmaṇa — unseen, of swift action — comes into being therein at once, the Lord who sets the body in motion.'

sanskrit: na vinā dhātusaṃghātaṃ śarīraṃ bhavati kva cit na ca jīvaṃ vinā brahman dhātavaś ceṣṭayanty uta
english: 'Nowhere does a body come to be without the assemblage of elements; nor, O brāhmaṇa, do the elements stir without the living self.'

sanskrit: sa jīvaḥ parisaṃkhyātaḥ śeṣaḥ saṃkarṣaṇaḥ prabhuḥ tasmāt sanatkumāratvaṃ yo labheta svakarmaṇā
english: 'That living self is reckoned to be Śeṣa, the Lord Saṃkarṣaṇa; from him one may attain, by his own works, the state of Sanatkumāra.'

sanskrit: yasmiṃś ca sarvabhūtāni pralayaṃ yānti saṃkṣaye sa manaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ pradyumnaḥ paripaṭhyate
english: 'And he into whom all beings pass at the dissolution — he, the mind of all creatures, is proclaimed to be Pradyumna.'

sanskrit: tasmāt prasūto yaḥ kartā kāryaṃ kāraṇam eva ca yasmāt sarvaṃ prabhavati jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam so 'niruddhaḥ sa īśāno vyaktiḥ sā sarvakarmasu
english: 'From him is born the doer who is both the effect and the cause, and from whom springs the whole world, moving and unmoving — he is Aniruddha, he is the Lord, the manifestation present in all works.'

sanskrit: yo vāsudevo bhagavān kṣetrajño nirguṇātmakaḥ jñeyaḥ sa eva bhagavāñ jīvaḥ saṃkarṣaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
english: 'He who is the Lord Vāsudeva, the Knower of the field, of nature free from qualities — that very Lord is to be known as the living self, the Lord Saṃkarṣaṇa.'

sanskrit: saṃkarṣaṇāc ca pradyumno manobhūtaḥ sa ucyate pradyumnād yo 'niruddhas tu so 'haṃkāro maheśvaraḥ
english: 'From Saṃkarṣaṇa comes Pradyumna, who is said to be of the nature of mind; and the Aniruddha who comes from Pradyumna is the principle of ego, the Great Lord.'

sanskrit: mattaḥ sarvaṃ saṃbhavati jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam akṣaraṃ ca kṣaraṃ caiva sac cāsac caiva nārada
english: 'From me arises the whole world, moving and unmoving — the imperishable and the perishable, the being and the non-being alike, O Nārada.'
